summary: What a portfolio decided about each project, programme or portfolio in it: its priority, and whether to invest in it, hold it or stop it.
example: This season: invest in the Quality Improvement Programme first; hold the member app until its pilot reports.
definition: The decisions a portfolio made at its latest review. For each project, programme or portfolio in it, you record a priority, a decision, the reason and the date. Invest means fund it and let it continue. Hold means keep it but commit nothing more until the next review. Stop means end it and free its budget and people.

/spec/portfolio.guide: The portfolio these decisions belong to.

/metadata/name.guide: A name for this set of decisions, usually the review it came from.

/spec/decisions.guide: One decision for each project, programme or portfolio in this portfolio.

/spec/decisions/-/kind.guide: Whether the decision is about a project, a programme or a portfolio.

/spec/decisions/-/id.guide: The project, programme or portfolio this decision is about. It must be in this portfolio.

/spec/decisions/-/priority.guide: Its rank: 1 is first. Two things may share a rank.

good: Moves the pass rate most for the least spend this season.

poor.why: Too vague. Say what it moves forward, or what has to change first.
